foundItems.title: What Can Translation Do?
foundItems.description: In a new blog post to mark International Translation Day 2026, World Writing in French series editors Charles Forsdick and Martin Munro reflect on translation's role in sustaining linguistic and literary diversity, and ask an urgent question: what can translation do?

foundItems.title: Oxford University Voltaire: a living edition
foundItems.description: Explore the latest updates to Oxford University Voltaire, the living digital edition of Voltaire’s complete works, with newly added content and ongoing enhancements for researchers and libraries.

foundItems.title: Liverpool University Press to publish Art Libraries Journal from 2027
foundItems.description: Liverpool University Press will become the new publisher of Art Libraries Journal from 2027, continuing the journal’s established legacy following its publication by Cambridge University Press.

foundItems.title: Revisiting Abercrombie’s ‘The Preservation of Rural England’ one hundred years on | Town Planning Review 97.5 Featured Article
foundItems.description: The editors of Town Planning Review have selected 'Revisiting Abercrombie’s ‘The Preservation of Rural England’ one hundred years on', by Mark Scott, Nick Gallent and Menelaos Gkartzios. as the Featured Article from Volume 97.5. Explore both the landmark text and this new centenary reassessment side by side, free to read for a limited time.

foundItems.title: The State Bibles
foundItems.description: The State Bibles: The Anglo-Dutch Politics of the King James Version and the Statenvertaling, by Esther van Raamsdonk, published by the British Academy, is the first extended comparative study of two key bible translations of the early modern period – the King James Version (1611) and the Dutch Statenvertaling (1637).
